string.text: A standard 20-gauge cartridge loaded with 6mm buckshot. At close range it has enormous lethal and stopping power. Intended for use only in smoothbore weapons.

The 5.7x28mm SS190 is a pistol cartridge developed in 1986 as a replacement for the 9x19mm Parabellum. Compared to the 9x19mm cartridge, it provides a flatter trajectory, reduced recoil, greater effective range, armor penetration, and a reduced tendency to ricochet. This cartridge occupies a niche between pistol and intermediate (assault rifle) cartridges. The 5.7x28mm cartridge is used in the FN P90 submachine gun (Personal Defense Weapon) and the FN Five-seveN pistol.
The 5.7x28 SS195 JHP is a hollow point cartridge with less penetration than the SS190, but greater stopping power and lethality.

.50 Action Express (also .50 AE, 12.7x33, 12.7x32.6mm) is a cartridge developed in 1988 for the Israeli Desert Eagle pistol. One of the most powerful self-contained pistol cartridges in the world. It has a flat-nosed bullet, which accounts for the enormous stopping power of this cartridge.
Magnum (Latin: Magnum, from magnus — large, great) is a high-powered cartridge compared to a standard cartridge of the same caliber. Also refers to a firearm chambered for this type of cartridge.
A Soviet pistol cartridge of 7.62mm caliber. A simple full metal jacket bullet with a lead core.
A Soviet pistol cartridge of 7.62mm caliber. A steel-core bullet with improved armor penetration.
A Soviet assault rifle cartridge of 7.62mm caliber (index 57-N-231). A simple jacketed bullet with a steel core.
A Soviet armor-piercing assault rifle cartridge of 7.62mm caliber (index 7N23). A bullet with a heat-hardened tool steel core, with improved armor penetration.
A NATO standard rifle cartridge. Caliber — 7.62mm. A simple jacketed bullet with a lead core.
A NATO standard armor-piercing rifle cartridge. Caliber — 7.62mm. A steel-core bullet with improved armor penetration.
The standard military sniper cartridge 7.62x54mm PS (index 7N1). The bullet features a flat-nosed steel core. An inexpensive-to-manufacture variant of the sniper cartridge for sniper rifles.

The updated model received the index AEK-919K.

The AK-104/AK-105 are modifications of the AK-103 and AK-74M respectively, with a barrel shortened by 101mm. The intermediate barrel length (between the AK-74M and AKS-74U) allowed the weapon's overall dimensions to be reduced while keeping the gas port in the same position relative to the breech end of the barrel as on the AK-74M, rather than moving it rearward (as on the AKS-74U). This improved parts commonality across the entire "100-series" family.

The rifle's action is based on a rotating bolt. The rifle belongs to the "anti-materiel" class, but is more commonly used as a weapon against enemy infantry.

The M16 (official designation: Rifle, Caliber 5.56mm, M16) is an American 5.56mm automatic rifle developed on the basis of the AR-15 and adopted in the 1960s. The M16 and its variants remain the primary armament of American infantry to this day. It is one of the most widely produced small arms in the world — over 8 million units have been manufactured.

The M16A1 is an improved variant of the M16. Key differences include the addition of a forward assist mechanism, an improved bolt carrier buffer (which reduced the rate of fire to 750–850 rounds per minute and eliminated bolt bounce and misfires), a more reliable closed-prong flash hider, chrome-lined bolt carrier (to prevent corrosion), a reduction in rifling twist from 356 to 305mm (which improved bullet stability but increased dispersion at ranges beyond 400m), and a bayonet lug. A 30-round magazine and a suppressor designed for use with standard (rather than subsonic) ammunition were also created specifically for the new rifle. It was in service with the US Army from 1967 to 1985.

The ranging scales are calibrated for shooting from 100m to 400m (in 50m increments). For twilight shooting, the scopes feature illuminated reticles. A standard AA battery is now used as the power source in place of the original 2RTs63 accumulator.
The PU (from Pritsel Ukorochenny — Shortened Scope) is a Soviet optical scope originally developed in 1940.
A 1939-production scope for the Mauser 98k rifle.
A sound suppressor for the PB pistol (6P9).
A sound suppressor for the SR-3M "Vikhr" assault rifle.
A suppressor from the OTs-14 "Groza" assault rifle/grenade launcher system delivery kit.
A sound suppressor for the VSK-94 rifle.
A sound suppressor for the FN Five-seveN pistol.
A sound suppressor for the APS and OTs-33 "Pernach" pistols.
A sound suppressor for .45-caliber pistols and submachine guns.

The ATG tactical assault rifle suppressor is designed to reduce the sound and muzzle flash when firing from 5.56mm Kalashnikov assault rifles AK101 and AK102, as well as 7.62mm Kalashnikov assault rifles AK103 and AK104.

The TGP-A-5.45 tactical suppressor/flash hider for 5.45mm AK-series assault rifles and RPK-74 light machine guns. The suppressor design contains no rubber obturator and does not require the use of subsonic ammunition. However, shooting accuracy is slightly reduced when it is installed.

The TGP-V tactical suppressor/flash hider for the SVD. It can be installed on the SVD over the standard slotted cylindrical flash hider. Its purpose is to provide concealment of the shooter's position (day and night), reduce the intensity of the muzzle report, and virtually eliminate muzzle flash. It also reduces the acoustic impact on the shooter (preventing concussion in enclosed spaces).
The Attenuator 5.7x28mm suppressor manufactured by Fabrique Nationale Herstal for the FN P90 submachine gun.
A muzzle sound moderator from Hexagon, designed for 12-gauge carbines and shotguns.

The Salvo 12 is a modular non-cylindrical suppressor that can be lengthened or shortened depending on the user's needs. The suppressor is claimed to be multi-purpose and equally useful for hunters, sport shooters, and those who choose a shotgun for home defense. Can be installed on the SPAS-12.
A very simple, budget-friendly yet already sufficiently effective muzzle brake/compensator for designs without enclosed reactive chambers. Can be installed on the OTs-02 "Kiparis."
An Izhmash-manufactured sound suppressor for earlier-generation Vityaz submachine guns.
A sound suppressor for the PP-2000 submachine gun.
A sound suppressor for the Kedr submachine gun.
A sound suppressor for the IMI Uzi submachine gun family.
PBS-1. A device for silent and flash-free firing from the 7.62mm Kalashnikov assault rifle. When the suppressor is fitted, firing is conducted using US subsonic cartridges.
PBS-4. A device for silent and flash-free firing from the 5.45mm compact Kalashnikov assault rifle (AKS-74U).
The AAC M4-2000 suppressor is designed for installation on most assault rifles and carbines chambered in 5.56x45mm.
The AAC 762-SDN-6 suppressor is designed for use with 7.62x51mm NATO cartridges.
The standard Izhmash-manufactured suppressor for the SV-98.
A suppressor for certain sniper rifles.

The GP-34 underbarrel grenade launcher was developed on the basis of the military GP-30 "Obuvka" grenade launcher in the early 2000s at the Izhmash design bureau. The new launcher (notably the first and only one developed at Izhmash) was designed as a competitor to the Tula GP-30M "Obuvka" and is intended for installation on full-size Kalashnikov assault rifles: AK-74M, the modern "100-series," AN-94 "Abakan," AEK-971, and the latest AK-12. It is in service with the Russian Armed Forces and Ministry of Internal Affairs, and is exported.

The M320 underbarrel grenade launcher was created to replace the M203. The Picatinny Arsenal held a competition for a new 40mm underbarrel grenade launcher, which was won by Heckler & Koch in early 2006. The M320 was developed on the basis of the Heckler & Koch AG36, though the two are not fully identical. Production began in November 2008. The launcher was officially presented in July 2009 at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, by the 1st Brigade of the 82nd Airborne Division.

An underbarrel grenade launcher developed by the German arms manufacturer Heckler & Koch to replace the HK 79. Its primary platform is the HK G36 rifle.

An underbarrel grenade launcher developed specifically for use with the L85A2 rifle. Designed to fire various types of 40mm underbarrel grenades in NATO service.

The FN40GL is a modification of the FN GL1 grenade launcher adapted for use with FN SCAR assault rifles. The FN40GL is a single-shot, rifled weapon built on the traditional sliding barrel design.

The 9A-91 uses a gas-operated action with gas tapped from the barrel. Locking is achieved by a rotating bolt with 4 locking lugs. The trigger mechanism is hammer-fired and allows both semi-automatic and fully automatic fire.

A Croatian submachine gun created during the early period of the Yugoslav Civil War. It was used by self-defense units, partisan/insurgent forces, and sabotage/terrorist formations, as well as by some Croatian army units, but was never officially adopted. The submachine gun proved popular among criminals, as the wartime-produced weapons were not test-fired for the Ministry of Internal Affairs ballistics database and (with the exception of a few display pieces) bore no markings whatsoever.

The 9mm Stechkin Automatic Pistol is an automatic pistol developed in the late 1940s to early 1950s by designer I. Ya. Stechkin and adopted by the Soviet Armed Forces in 1951, simultaneously with the Makarov pistol. The APS is intended to arm officers directly participating in combat operations, as well as soldiers and sergeants of certain special units.

The 9mm modernized Makarov pistol PMM (GRAU index — 56-A-125M) is a Russian pistol developed in the early 1990s under the "Grach" R&D program. It participated in the competition for a new military pistol under the designation "Grach-3."
The 8x57 IS cartridge was the primary cartridge of the German Army during World War I and World War II.

The most widely used cartridge in the German Army was the heavy pointed bullet s.S (schweres Spitzgeschoss) round, with a bullet weight of 12.8 grams. It was intended for use in heavy and light machine guns, rifles, and carbines in service with the Wehrmacht.
Originally developed as a specialized long-range sniper cartridge, it is today also widely used by hunters and sport shooters.

The 12.7x55mm STs-130 is a Russian rifle cartridge with a subsonic bullet, developed at TsKIB SOO for the low-noise and flash-free engagement of protected targets and personnel in heavy body armor at ranges of up to 600 meters.

The 12.7x99mm (also known as ".50 BMG" and "12.7x99mm NATO") is a large-caliber cartridge used by NATO armies. It was developed in the 1920s as ammunition for the Browning M1921 heavy machine gun. After World War II the cartridge was standardized within NATO and is produced by various member nations to unified technical specifications.

A special sniper cartridge. It has a subsonic muzzle velocity, making it suitable for use in suppressed weapons during special operations. Thanks to its caliber it offers high stopping power, and its heavy specially designed bullet penetrates most body armor at ranges of up to 200 meters.

An armor-piercing cartridge with enhanced penetration. The bullet incorporates a hardened tool steel armor-piercing core. Designed to engage personnel behind light armored cover at ranges of up to 500m.

The 40mm VOG-25P round, also known as "Podkidysh" (7P24), is a fragmentation grenade for grenade launchers whose primary distinguishing feature is a nose fuze that causes the grenade to bounce off the ground and detonate in the air, increasing its lethality.
